invariants.statement: Gate 1 contains no runtime implementation and Gate 2 can emit ALLOW only.
Only exact user-enrolled HTTPS Canvas origins can become recognized surfaces; wildcards and all-URL access are rejected.
Cookies, headers, bodies, queries, fragments, credentials, authorization material, answers, grades, course content, student identifiers, and full browsing history are never captured or persisted.
Unknown, inconsistent, stale, or conflicting inputs always allow traffic and disable future enforcement.
A suspected or unknown assessment surface dominates every tab and window in its browser context and suspends request observation.
Essential, assessment, authentication or SSO, autosave or submission, security, same-origin batched, and unknown traffic are never altered.
Private browsing is inactive at the product layer in Gate 2 and produces no persistent state or records.
Startup, update, restart, and service-worker wake reconstruct state from current permissions and tabs before observation becomes active.
Emergency disable immediately stops observation, clears volatile state, and requires explicit user re-enable.
The product has no telemetry, remote diagnostics, cloud sync, accounts, remote rules, or remote code.
SSO transit never broadens permissions, observes identity-provider traffic, records URLs, or implies successful authentication.
Tab and window membership is reference-counted per browser context; removal of one surface cannot deactivate another.
Same-origin, payload-dependent, or batched traffic cannot be classified as optional-separable.
Permission loss or mismatch stops observation and clears any future session rules before another state is shown.
Persistent records are local, capped at 500, time-bucketed, deleted within 24 hours, and user-deletable immediately.
The reducer is pure, deterministic, idempotent for equivalent snapshots, and independent of event delivery order after reconciliation.
A future rule cannot be enforced without a separately accepted rule authorization record and Gate 3 implementation evidence.
Every dependency and copied file requires provenance and file-level license review; GPL, AGPL, or MPL implementation code is not copied into PolyForm-only files.
